summary: Four-lane audit of the Iron Sunset RTS build + source-material art-style research

categories.name: infantry
categories.currentStyle: Pure top-down overhead sprites (helmet/backpack seen from directly above), 150-180px sources, painted-soft AI look with decent material texture but almost no readable anatomy. USA units olive-green, GLA tan robes (good), worker is a cartoon yellow hardhat blob. Drawn unrotated from 8 pre-baked facings; gait faked with lateral sway.
gapsVsSource: Camera is straight overhead, not the source's 3/4 high angle — no head/shoulder/legs silhouette; every unit reads as a colored blob with a stick gun at gameplay scale
Faction identity broken for China: redguard is olive-green (indistinguishable from USA ranger); hunter is green/dark with only tiny red bits — no China red trim
Per-facing camera mixing inside single sheets: terrorist frames 5-7 and rpg frame 6 are 3/4 standing figures while other frames are pure overhead (verified in _ws_a2_montage.png)
Worker reads toy-like/emoji-ish (giant yellow hardhat), off the gritty-military register
Style clash with the side-profile painted vehicles they fight next to
No team-color/house-color accent for ownership readability

categories.name: vehicles
categories.currentStyle: Two unrelated art generations. (A) USA/China hero vehicles (crusader...nukecannon, ~140-160px): handsome painted SIDE-PROFILE sprites with baked drop shadows, strong faction palettes (USA blue-grey, China red w/ stars and 龙 markings). (B) All nine GLA combat vehicles (technical, quad, scorpion, marauder, buggy, toxin, scud, cycle, bombtruck): 64x64 dark top-down pixel-art minis in a completely different style and scale. Plus odd singles: truck/battlebus side-view, bulldozer photo-like on a semi-transparent white box, separate 'dozer' duplicate.
gapsVsSource: Camera elevation flips per facing within one unit: E/W frames are side profile, N/S frames are top-down (verified crusader rotation strip) — the tank changes perspective as it turns, the classic AI-sheet artifact; source uses one consistent 3/4 camera
Entire GLA vehicle roster is a different art generation: tiny, dark, top-down 64px pixel sprites vs 140px painted USA/China — the faction literally looks like a different game

Sheet-slicing contamination: inferno_0 and nukecannon_0 carry a large dark hull fragment from the adjacent sheet cell at frame top; overlord_0 and battlemaster_0 have smaller stray fragments (verified in _audit_zoom_chinatops.png)
bulldozer_0 has 64% semi-transparent pixels — the white background was alpha-faded, not removed, so it renders inside a ghost white box; also duplicates the separate 'dozer' asset
Baked drop shadows are inconsistent in direction/strength across sprites and absent on the GLA minis
Side profile is not the source's 3/4 high-angle; hulls show no top surfaces so they don't sit on top-down terrain convincingly

categories.name: aircraft
categories.currentStyle: Split style. Jets (raptor grey, aurora blue, mig red) are painted side/3-4 profile sprites at good fidelity with baked shadows. Helicopters (comanche, chinook) are pure top-down, washed-out olive: comanche is a faint pale silhouette (25% opaque), chinook is essentially a flat olive rectangle with two rotor circles (see _verify.png).
gapsVsSource: Helicopters vs jets use different cameras (top-down vs side) and wildly different fidelity — chinook has almost no painted detail, no panel lines, no rotor blur, no shadow
Jet sheets have the same per-facing elevation flip as vehicles (raptor N/S frames go top-down, E/W side)
No rotor animation frames / motion cue for helicopters; they read as static decals
MiG's bright toy-red saturation is hotter than the source's gritty military finish (minor)

categories.name: buildings
categories.currentStyle: The strongest category: consistent near-plan-view (slight high-angle) painted sprites, ~320px, with 3 damage states each, good greeble density and painted-texture fidelity. Market (GLA junk tarps), palace (gold), propaganda (red/black) carry faction flavor.
gapsVsSource: Camera is near-straight-down roof view — source shows building facades at 3/4, which is what sells scale; most of these read as detailed roofs

Faction identity weak on shared greys: bunker, def, nuke, strategy, hq, power, particle all read neutral grey-tech — a China nuke plant and a USA strategy center would look interchangeable; no faction tint or house-color trim
tunnel is an off-style outlier: soft 3D-render look, different lighting/palette, and a 587x317 wide footprint vs everyone else's ~320px square
Style clash with the flat vector terrain/decor they sit on (painted roofs on programmer-art ground)
No build-up/construction art implied by asset set (only damage states)

categories.name: terrain/decor
categories.currentStyle: Fully procedural flat-color canvas: single biome base color + 2-octave value-noise mottle + a visible 4.5%-alpha tile grid, roads as stroked lines with 2 wheel-rut lines, cliffs as 2px dark rims on blocked tiles, water as per-tile rectangles with shimmer ellipses, and decor drawn as vector primitives (trees = 2 circles, shrubs = 5 circles, cactus = rectangles, rocks = 2 polygons). Desert/steppe/badlands palettes are hue-appropriate.
gapsVsSource: Zero painted texture — the source's ground is photographic/painted tiling texture with detail maps; this is flat vector noise and it undercuts every painted sprite placed on it
Blocked terrain/'cliffs' are just outlined tiles — no cliff faces, no elevation illusion
Vector-primitive trees/rocks/cacti clash hard with the painted buildings beside them
Visible alignment grid over the whole map reads as debug rendering
Water is tile-quantized rectangles with hard shorelines, not blended shore transitions
No scorch marks, craters, debris, or environmental storytelling props (the roads+ruts are the one good gritty touch)

categories.name: UI/HUD
categories.currentStyle: Cohesive dark-olive military CSS theme (panel rgba(18,21,14), border #4a5238, gold #e8c060) with Segoe UI font. Topbar = emoji stats (💰 ⚡ 🪖) + emoji buttons (🔊 ⏸ ❓ 🐞 🏗️). Sidebar = minimap canvas + 3-column build grids whose buttons use a 20px emoji glyph + 9px text label. Start screen = plain text faction cards + text difficulty buttons, gold-glow title.
gapsVsSource: Emoji iconography everywhere is the single biggest tone-breaker — source uses painted unit-cameo portrait buttons; emoji reads 'web app', not war room, and renders differently per OS
Segoe UI body font and generic rounded CSS buttons; no stencil/military display face, no metal bevel/rivet framing that defines the source's sidebar and radar
Build buttons have no unit imagery at all — players learn icons, and 20px emoji cannot carry 30+ unit identities
Start-screen faction cards are text-only: no faction emblems, no key art
No command-bar portrait/veterancy area for the selected unit (selInfo is plain text)
Minimap has a plain 1px border — no radar housing/frame

crossCutting: Camera anarchy is the #1 issue: side-profile hero vehicles + pure-overhead infantry/helicopters + plan-view buildings + top-down terrain all share one battlefield; the source's identity is ONE consistent 3/4 high-angle camera for everything

Perspective flips WITHIN single 8-frame sheets: E/W facings are side-view, N/S facings top-down (crusader, raptor confirmed; pattern is generation-wide), so units visibly change camera as they rotate in-game

At least four coexisting art generations: painted side-view hero vehicles, 64px pixel-art GLA minis, rotation-derived overhead infantry, plus procedural vector fallback units and vector decor — GLA in particular looks imported from another game

Faction palette drift: factions are crisp on vehicles (blue-grey/red/tan) but collapse on infantry (China redguard is USA-olive) and buildings (shared neutral greys), and there is no house-color/team-tint system anywhere
Shadow inconsistency: baked drop shadows of varying direction on painted sprites, procedural ellipses on vector fallbacks, none on GLA minis
Scale/resolution spread: 64px GLA vehicles vs 140-160px USA/China vehicles vs 150-180px infantry vs 320px buildings vs 587px-wide tunnel outlier
Asset hygiene defects visible in-game: sheet-cut contamination blobs (inferno, nukecannon, overlord, battlemaster), bulldozer ghost-white halo, redundant bulldozer/dozer pair, near-untextured chinook
In-world painted art vs flat-CSS-and-emoji UI is a constant register clash on every frame
topFixes: 1. Asset hygiene sweep (hours, removes visible garbage): erase the contamination blobs on inferno_0/nukecannon_0/overlord_0/battlemaster_0, hard-key the bulldozer white halo to true alpha, delete one of bulldozer/dozer, and clamp the MiG saturation — pure cleanup, zero regeneration risk

2. Regenerate the 9 GLA vehicles (technical, quad, scorpion, marauder, buggy, toxin, scud, cycle, bombtruck) at 140px in the same painted style/camera as the USA/China vehicles — one batch job that makes an entire faction stop looking like a different game
3. Repaint chinook + comanche as detailed 3/4 sprites at raptor/mig fidelity (chinook is currently a flat olive rectangle) — 2 assets, huge per-asset payoff since aircraft are large on screen

4. Fix per-facing camera flips: regenerate N/S(+diagonal) frames of the vehicle/jet sheets so every facing holds one 3/4 high angle — kills the 'tank changes perspective while turning' artifact that undermines otherwise-good sprites

5. Re-shoot infantry as 3/4 high-angle sprites with readable head/shoulder/gun silhouettes (and fix the mixed standing frames in terrorist/rpg); recolor redguard/hunter with China red trim while at it — restores both silhouette readability and faction ID in one batch

6. UI icon pass: replace all emoji (topbar stats, build buttons, mobile buttons) with a small drawn military icon set or 1-frame unit-cameo crops from existing sprites, and swap headers to a stencil display font — CSS layout stays, tone transforms

7. Terrain texture pass: overlay a tiling painted detail texture (sand grain, cracked earth) on the noise base, remove the visible tile grid, and blend water shorelines — code-only change in renderTerrain, upgrades every screenshot
8. Replace vector decor with painted sprite decor (3-4 trees, 2 rocks, cactus, wreck/crater props) matching building fidelity — small asset batch, fixes the worst painted-on-programmer-art clash

9. Add a house-color/team-tint accent system (colored trim stripe or canopy tint on all units + flag/light on buildings) — restores the source's ownership readability and papers over remaining palette drift

10. Normalize shadows: strip baked sprite shadows and draw one consistent runtime ellipse shadow (single global light direction) for all units/aircraft — makes the mixed-generation assets sit on the same ground plane

findings.title: deploy.ps1: failed Firebase deploy is never retried (copy-then-deploy mtime trap)
findings.detail: The script copies generals-zero-hour.html to public/index.html BEFORE running firebase deploy. If the deploy fails (network, auth, quota), the next run's mtime gate sees src <= dst and prints 'source unchanged, skipping deploy' forever — the failure is silently never retried until someone remembers -Force. Also, edits to sw.js, manifest.json, or assets alone never trigger a deploy at all (only the html mtime is compared), and public/assets is copy-only, never pruned, so deleted/renamed sprites keep shipping. Move the copy after a successful deploy (or write a .last-deployed marker), include sw.js/manifest/assets mtimes in the gate, and mirror-delete stale files in public/assets.
findings.anchor: deploy.ps1 Firebase block, lines 19–37 (mtime gate line 20–22, Copy-Item line 26, firebase deploy line 36)

findings.title: Full-map offscreen canvases (~315MB on Large) risk iOS canvas eviction/crash
findings.detail: renderTerrain allocates terrCanvas at WW×WH (5120×5120 = ~105MB RGBA on Large 128²), and buildWaterFrames allocates TWO more full-map canvases (~210MB) even though only 4–12 pond tiles per frame are painted. Total canvas backing approaches or exceeds mobile Safari's canvas memory budget, so the stated DoD 'PWA verified on a real phone' will hit blank canvases or tab reloads on Large maps. Water frames should be tiny per-pond canvases (or drawn tile-by-tile each frame), and terrain could be chunked or drawn with a source-rect.

findings.title: Single save slot: autosave clobbers manual saves, and starting a new match wipes the old save instantly
findings.detail: Manual save, 60s autosave, and Continue all share SAVE_KEY 'bg_save'. A deliberate pause-menu save is overwritten by the next autosave (possibly seconds before a defeat), and because _autosaveT starts at 0 and is never reset in startGame, clicking START WAR writes an autosave on the first tick — instantly destroying the previous campaign's save the Continue button pointed at. Split into 'bg_save_auto' and 'bg_save_manual' (Continue offers newest) or at least don't autosave in the first minute.

findings.title: deserialize() destroys the live match before validating the save
findings.detail: deserialize calls resetMatchState() first, then parses base64 arrays and rebuilds entities; if anything throws mid-way (corrupt/truncated localStorage, bad def ref), loadSaveFromStorage catches it — but the running match is already wiped (units/buildings cleared, G.state='menu'), leaving the player stuck behind the pause menu over a dead canvas. Same family: genMap() can throw 'reachability guarantee failed' and no startGame/restartMatch call site catches it. Parse and validate the whole save into detached structures first, and only then swap game state; wrap genMap with a retry/toast.
findings.anchor: deserialize (line ~2865, resetMatchState call at ~2867); loadSaveFromStorage (~2955); genMap throw (~687)

findings.title: G.upgrades.warCollege leaks across matches (never reset)
findings.detail: startGame resets perks/stats/ai but not G.upgrades, and resetMatchState doesn't touch it either. Once a USA player completes the Officer Academy, warCollege=true persists for every subsequent match in the session — new USA matches get +40% sniper range (getEffectiveRange) from t=0 without building the academy. It's also serialized, so the flag can ride through save/load into fresh matches. One-line fix: reset G.upgrades in startGame/resetMatchState.
findings.anchor: startGame (line ~2728–2731) vs G.upgrades init (line ~632); set in updateBuilding (~1360); read in getEffectiveRange (~1173)

findings.title: Buildings under construction shrug off damage: hp is overwritten by the build-progress formula and completion full-heals
findings.detail: updateBuild sets b.hp = maxHp*0.1 + maxHp*0.9*(prog/t) every tick a builder works the site, erasing any damage dealt between ticks — attackers can only kill a worked site with single-frame burst. Worse, the completion line b.hp=Math.min(maxHp, Math.max(b.hp, maxHp)) always evaluates to maxHp, so a building shelled to 15% during construction pops out at 100%. Track damage separately (e.g. b.dmgTaken) and subtract it from the progress-derived hp, and drop the Math.max on completion.
findings.anchor: updateBuild (line ~1558) and the !b.done completion branch in updateBuilding (line ~1358)

findings.title: Autosave is a synchronous multi-hundred-KB JSON stringify every 60s — mid-battle hitch and localStorage quota risk
findings.detail: serialize() base64-encodes four full map arrays and serializes every unit including its complete waypoint path with unrounded float coordinates; late-game on Large maps this is easily 1MB+, stringified and written to localStorage synchronously inside the update loop — a visible frame hitch once a minute during the biggest fights, and a real shot at QuotaExceeded (5MB cap) which makes autosave silently stop. Round coordinates, drop paths (recompute on load from dest), and consider deferring the stringify to an idle callback.

findings.title: Target acquisition and splash damage still O(units×entities) — the spatial grid is only used for separation/horde
findings.detail: acquire() (every 0.3–0.35s per scanning unit), the building defense scan, and splashDamage all iterate ALL units + buildings with Math.hypot. Fine at the measured 300-unit scale, but it's the remaining quadratic wall: it will dominate the planned WS-B6 headless faster-than-realtime balance sims and any future battle-size increase. SGRID already exists but contains only units — extend queries to acquisition (iterate cells within sight radius) and add a static building index (buildings rarely move).
findings.anchor: acquire (line ~1157), building scan in updateBuilding (line ~1390), splashDamage (line ~1092), SGRID (line ~1473)

findings.title: sw.js precache list is a hand-maintained duplicate of UNIT_SPRITE_REG — drift silently breaks offline
findings.detail: UNIT_KEYS and BLD_KEYS in sw.js must be kept in sync with UNIT_SPRITE_REG and BLD_SPRITES in the HTML by hand (the comment admits it). Any new unit/building sprite added in one place but not the other ships fine online but 404s offline — exactly the failure mode the PWA DoD tests last. Fix cheaply: have deploy.ps1 generate the list into sw.js from the assets folder (it already globs *_[0-7].png), or drop precache enumeration and let the runtime cache-fill cover sprites.
findings.anchor: sw.js UNIT_KEYS/BLD_KEYS (lines 13–25) vs UNIT_SPRITE_REG (html line ~2134) and BLD_SPRITES key list (~2150)

findings.title: Targeting/input modes are scattered flags with superweapon firing triplicated — direct friction for WS-B2 Generals' Powers
findings.detail: G.placing, G.amoveMode, swTargeting, G.wallDrag, and touch.mode are five ad-hoc, mutually-exclusive-by-convention mode flags checked independently in mousedown, mouseup, keydown (Esc priority chain), and the touch path; superweapon click-to-fire is implemented three separate times (mouseup swTargeting branch, issueCommand sup branch, touchTap sup branch). WS-B2 adds nine targeted powers with cursors and AI casting — a fourth copy per path. Consolidating into one 'active targeting mode' object (cursor, validate, commit callbacks) before B2 would cut that work roughly in half and kill the desync bugs between desktop and touch.
findings.anchor: swTargeting (line ~1736), issueCommand super branch (~1786), mouseup branch (~1889), touchTap (~2009–2018), Esc chain (~2040)

findings.title: AI superweapon (and attack waves) target random player buildings including $60 wall segments
findings.detail: updateBuilding's AI auto-fire does pick(myBuildings(0)) with no filter, so the enemy nuke/Helios/Tempest — a ~95–100s cooldown weapon — can be spent on a single wall tile; wave targeting has the same blind pick. Building walls thus passively defuses AI supers. Filter out b.def.wall (the win-check already does) and weight by cost or def.super/production value.
findings.anchor: AI super fire in updateBuilding (line ~1370, pick(myBuildings(0))); wave targeting in aiTick (~1725)

findings.title: No devicePixelRatio handling — the whole game renders blurry on retina/mobile screens
findings.detail: resize() sets canvas.width=innerWidth in CSS pixels, so on a DPR 2–3 phone (the WS-B3 mobile push target) sprites, text, and the minimap are upscaled and soft — undermining the sprite-quality work Track A just shipped. Fix by sizing the backing store at innerWidth*dpr with ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0); the camera/input math already works in CSS pixels so the change is mostly contained to resize() and the two fillRect calls that use canvas.width.

sourceStyleTraits: Camera: fixed-pitch perspective bird's-eye at CameraPitch=37.5 deg default (GameData.ini), yaw mostly locked, limited zoom band — at gameplay height it reads near-axonometric. For 2D sprites: render every asset at one locked ~40-50 deg elevation, one yaw per facing, sun always from the same upper-left azimuth.

Overall rendering: gritty desaturated realism — dusty atmosphere, wear-and-tear grime painted onto every unit/building texture; a big leap from the saturated cartoon look of Red Alert 2. Muted mid-contrast grade, warm sun key light, no fog/DOF at gameplay zoom (uniform sharpness).

USA faction palette: light metallic gray hulls, blue-tinted accents, white star decals, clean high-tech silhouettes (Comanches, drones, particle-beam glow cyan/white); bright metallic gray installations.

China faction palette: dull olive-drab green vehicles with red trim/red star iconography, heavy riveted industrial mass (bulky twin-barrel tanks), buildings with pagoda-inspired reddish roofs; napalm/black-smoke warm FX.
GLA faction palette: khaki/sand + rust + improvised scrap-metal look, tarps and welded plates, Arabian sandstone/mudbrick buildings, no power infrastructure, toxin-green accent FX.

Texture fidelity: low-res (roughly 256-512px per object) hand-painted-over-photo textures with baked-in ambient occlusion and grime — chunky readable detail, not photoreal noise. This 'painted photo' texture crunch is the core of the 2003 look and is easy to emulate with slight blur + detail LoRA restraint.

Shadows: simple hard projected/planar shadows in one consistent direction; buildings visually anchored by their shadow. For sprites: bake one shared drop-shadow pass (same angle, same opacity) rather than per-image AI shadows.

Building silhouettes: squat, wide-footprint, instantly readable at small size; each has one animated landmark feature (radar dish spin, flag, smoke stack, arcing tesla-style glow) and faction-specific architecture language.

Unit proportions: slightly exaggerated turrets/weapons vs hull and oversized infantry relative to vehicles, tuned for readability at RTS zoom; player/team color appears as small decal trims (house-color patches), not whole-unit tint.

Terrain: tiled photographic dirt/desert/grass with visible tiling and splat-blended transitions, road splines, scorch/crater decals; theaters skew arid (desert, steppe, urban rubble) — a sandy-khaki global palette bias.
FX language: copious particles — dust puffs on movement, muzzle flashes, oily black smoke columns, tracer lines, big orange fireball explosions with debris; explosions linger as scorch decals.

UI: full-width bottom command bar (Generals dropped the classic C&C right sidebar) — radar/minimap left, context-sensitive build/command cameo-button grid center, selected-unit portrait right, cash + power readouts; beveled metallic frame reskinned per faction; cameo icons are small painted renders with dark outlines in colored frames.

replicationTechniques.how: One shared prompt scaffold for every asset: 'aerial three-quarter military RTS unit render, seen from 40 degrees above, gritty realistic 2003 video game style, desaturated dusty palette, hard sunlight from upper left, plain neutral background' + per-faction palette clause (USA gray/blue, China olive/red, GLA khaki/rust). Same checkpoint (juggernautXL or dreamshaperXL Turbo, both on disk), same sampler settings, fixed negative prompt. This alone gets 70% of set-consistency.

Draw (or auto-derive via canny/scribble from existing sprites) a silhouette/lineart per unit, run through controlnet-union-sdxl-promax (installed) or the SD1.5 v1.1 canny/scribble/lineart models (all installed) with the style prompt. Guarantees on-model outline, footprint, and facing while the model paints the Generals-style surface. comfyui_controlnet_aux preprocessors are installed.

Instruction-edit every EXISTING sprite: 'repaint this sprite in gritty desaturated 2003 military RTS style, keep the pose, silhouette, proportions and background transparency'. qwen-image-edit-2511-Q4_K_M.gguf + Lightning 4-step LoRA are installed and this exact model is validated in two prior projects (photo restoration T2b, pixel-art walk cycles). Commercial-safe license, unlike Flux Kontext (also installed, but FLUX-dev is non-commercial — do not use for Iron Sunset since it's monetization-bound).

Run existing sprites through img2img at denoise 0.35-0.55 with the locked prompt template (+ optional style LoRA). Keeps layout/pose, swaps surface style. Cheapest batch pass; combine with ControlNet tile/canny from the source sprite to prevent drift on small assets.

replicationTechniques.technique: IPAdapter style transfer from your own anchor renders
replicationTechniques.how: Generate 3-5 'hero' renders that nail the look, then feed them as style references via IPAdapter so every subsequent generation inherits palette/grit/lighting. The ComfyUI_IPAdapter_plus node IS installed and the required CLIP-ViT-H-14 encoder IS in clip_vision, but only FaceID weights are on disk — download ip-adapter-plus_sdxl_vit-h.safetensors (free, ~850MB, huggingface.co/h94/IP-Adapter) into models/ipadapter. One file away from working.

replicationTechniques.technique: C&C Generals style LoRA from Civitai
replicationTechniques.how: 'Command and Conquer Generals Style F1D + XL' (civitai.com/models/1475301, SDXL + Flux versions, trigger word 'cinematic', free download) — use the SDXL version at low weight (0.5-0.7) for mood/palette/grading. IP caveat: it is trained on EA screenshots, so use it for atmosphere and grading only; never prompt it toward specific EA units, and eyeball outputs for accidental trade-dress reproduction before shipping. Related: Red Alert style (models/307548), GDI/NOD SD1.5 (models/81160), isometric game assets (models/328173), Mobile Game Isometric Building XL (models/1857872).

replicationTechniques.technique: 3D-proxy render pipeline (how the original actually did it)
replicationTechniques.how: Generate rough low-poly models (Meshy — installed, 1074 credits; or Blender MCP), screenshot at a fixed 37.5-deg camera in Blender for perfect 8-facing consistency, then run the screenshots through the img2img/Qwen gritty pass. Highest consistency for vehicles with turret facings, most setup effort; Meshy credits are finite (needs-purchase when exhausted).

replicationTechniques.technique: Train an own-style LoRA once the set converges
replicationTechniques.how: After unifying 20-40 sprites, train a lightweight SDXL LoRA on YOUR OWN outputs (local train_* tooling exists via the comfyui MCP: train_prepare_dataset/train_start) so future units land on-style in one shot. IP-clean because the training set is your own art. GPU-hours on the RTX 3080 and dataset-captioning effort; first run will need debugging.

Every sprite exits through the same code path: background removal (ComfyUI-RMBG installed / rembg benchmarked at 0.9s), Ultimate SD Upscale (installed) + 4x-UltraSharp then downscale to target sprite size for crispness, one shared LUT/color-grade + identical drop-shadow (fixed angle/opacity) applied in the browser-game-builder sprite scripts. A shared grade+shadow pass hides most residual AI style variance.

ipGuardrails: DO copy the genre conventions freely: ~37.5-45 deg locked RTS camera, gritty desaturated modern-military rendering, faction color-coding (gray/blue high-tech vs olive/red industrial vs khaki/rust improvised), bottom command bar with minimap-left/buttons-center/portrait-right, cameo-icon build buttons, power/cash economy HUD. Camera angles, palettes, UI layouts, and mechanics are not protectable expression.

DON'T reproduce EA's specific unit/building trade dress: no recognizable one-to-one silhouettes of signature designs (e.g., the Overlord twin-barrel tank with deck add-ons, Particle Cannon uplink ring, Scud Storm launcher cluster, Chinook/Comanche-styled USA airframes as drawn in Generals). Redesign each unit's silhouette from the generic military archetype (a 'heavy twin-barrel tank' is fine; EA's exact proportions/greebles are not) — the clone-forge mechanics-vs-expression rule.

DON'T use any names, marks, or audio: 'Command & Conquer', 'Generals', 'Zero Hour', 'GLA', EVA/announcer lines, mission text, logos, or fonts styled like the C&C logotype. Iron Sunset already has a re-skin grep gate (task #9) — add these strings to it, and never mention C&C in store listing copy (parallel to the existing no-DigitalNC listing rule).

DON'T ship raw outputs of C&C-trained LoRAs unreviewed: the Civitai Generals LoRA (models/1475301) is trained on EA screenshots — use it at low weight for palette/atmosphere only, never prompt it for named EA units, and run a human similarity pass on every shipped sprite; if an output is identifiable as a specific EA asset, regenerate. Prefer graduating to a LoRA trained on your OWN unified sprites, which is IP-clean.

DON'T extract or trace anything from the game files, mods, or OpenSAGE-loaded assets (the engine reimplementation is open source; the art/audio assets remain EA's), and don't use C&C box art/screenshots in Iron Sunset marketing or store pages.

DO keep the existing house rules in force for the new art: no real-world corporate logos or military unit insignia on units/buildings (CLAUDE.md apparel IP guardrail generalizes), and avoid real aircraft/vehicle manufacturer names in unit descriptions — generic archetype names only.
